parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no border/document exposure, no universal facility or custody rule documented, and protective machinery exists: anti-discrimination law covering goods and services, hate-speech provisions and penalty enhancements, plus state protection of Pride (police held back rock-throwing opponents). But enforcement is uneven — prosecutors downgrade hate-crime charges to misdemeanours — and societal hostility is documented and recent: 222+ online hate-speech incidents (2023), physical attacks on a gender-nonconforming person, 51% closeted (2018), and a 2011 Pride cancelled after attacks. This is tier-3 societal hostility with partial, uneven recourse rather than a tier-1 state exposure. Nothing shows the hostility reaching visitors in services directly, but the documented climate means a visibly non-conforming traveller carries real street-friction risk. Restrictive legal gender recognition is resident-facing and not counted.
